industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying a view that moved inside the industry this week: Software B2B Enterprise goes to Neutral on the rotation into software, Semiconductors stays Underweight on the AI capital spending re-pricing, Hardware stays Neutral with the evidence moved against it at the margin. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the market has stopped paying for AI capital spending (hyperscaler prints gave no lift, ABB sold on data-centre orders) while demand is intact and sub-sector upgrades continue (memory, equipment, power electronics), and the software-against-semiconductors factor pair is reversing (Goldman Sachs' desk, 26 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: B now, B prior. The industry row stays C because the industry is split by the rotation itself. Counter-case for D: the Nasdaq down 6% in two weeks with momentum down 15% is a regime statement about this industry; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

sector.why: Neutral, from Underweight, because the thematics read turned: the broadening trade has moved into software. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): Nordic software 'is working again', up 9% in a month as AI-disruption fears faded while hardware gives back gains (Danske Bank TMT, 27 October), and Goldman Sachs' desk (26 October) reports the software-against-semiconductors factor pair reversing, so two houses now describe the same rotation; against it the discount-rate case still holds (the US ten-year above 5%, the Fed hiking in December) and one software sector is not another (Fortinet down 20%, ServiceNow down 16%, cybersecurity broken; Outset Global, 29 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: A now, C prior, the market now ranks the sector first. Balanced, so Neutral by judgement, not Overweight: a row valued off a yield cannot be Overweight with the ten-year above 5%. Seven Pool names (Sinch and Sectra in the top twelve of the starting score, QT Group, Truecaller, Yubico, Planisware, SAP). Counter-case: the recovery is one month old in one region and the discount rate is rising. To B if the Fed path is marked down with relative strength holding A or B; back to D if relative strength falls to C with the ten-year still above 5%.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No Swedish survey and no Riksbank reading reached the pack this week, so the condition for B (a confidence print at or above normal with the Riksbank on hold) could not be tested; the only Swedish data point is food retail volumes up 5.3% in September after a value-added tax cut (Danske, 18 Oct), which is a sector fact, not a country view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Four live holdings are Swedish (Avanza 0.50%, Hexatronic 4.95%, Sdiptech 5.05%, Xvivo 5.05%, 15.55 points), judged in component 4 and in amendment 10. Relative strength is not graded by country.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
